skill.name: javascript-sdk
skill.description: Guides JavaScript and TypeScript integration with the inference.sh SDK for apps, agents, streaming, files, sessions, tools, and server proxies.
skill.summary: Build inference.sh applications and agents with JavaScript or TypeScript.
skill.author: inferen-sh

security_audit.summary: Most static matches are documentation syntax or legitimate SDK examples, including template literals, file operations, and server-side environment configuration. Confirmed risks include direct eval of agent input, an unpinned external skill install, broad package execution permissions, agent-callable webhooks, and a browser-exposed API key example.

remediation.issue: Agent-provided calculator expressions are passed to eval().
remediation.suggestion: Replace eval with a maintained expression parser and allow only required arithmetic operators and numeric inputs.

remediation.issue: The skill grants wildcard package-manager and Node command access.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict allowed tools to exact required commands, pin package versions, and require confirmation before installing external skills.

remediation.issue: A development example exposes an API key through NEXT_PUBLIC_INFERENCE_API_KEY.
remediation.suggestion: Remove direct browser authentication and route all requests through a server proxy that reads a private environment variable.

remediation.issue: Webhook tools can create model-directed outbound side effects.
remediation.suggestion: Require human approval, restrict destination hosts, validate payload fields, and avoid placing sensitive conversation content in webhook messages.

content.user_title: Build Apps with the inference.sh JavaScript SDK
content.value_statement: JavaScript teams need clear patterns for adding hosted AI tasks and agents. This skill provides SDK guidance for execution, streaming, files, tools, sessions, and proxies.
actual_capabilities: Explains installation and authentication for the @inferencesh/sdk package.
Shows synchronous, asynchronous, and streaming AI application execution.
Guides template-based and custom agents with tool calls and approval workflows.
Covers file uploads, generated file downloads, sessions, and conversation state.
Provides server proxy patterns for Next.js, Express, Hono, Remix, and SvelteKit.
Documents TypeScript types, React integration, error handling, and tool construction.
limitations: Requires an inference.sh account, API key, network access, and compatible application identifiers.
Examples require security review before production use, especially eval, webhooks, and browser credentials.
The skill does not guarantee model availability, pricing, response quality, or application schema stability.
Framework examples are reference patterns and may need adaptation for existing authentication and deployment systems.

use_cases.title: Add AI Tasks to Node.js
use_cases.description: Create a typed server integration that runs inference.sh applications and handles results, errors, and files.

use_cases.title: Build a Streaming React Interface
use_cases.description: Connect a React or Next.js interface through a server proxy and display incremental task progress.

use_cases.title: Create an Approved Tool Agent
use_cases.description: Design an agent with typed tools, sessions, and human confirmation for sensitive external actions.

prompt_templates.title: Install and Run a Task
prompt_templates.prompt: Set up @inferencesh/sdk in my Node.js project. Show a minimal task call using a server-side environment variable and explain each required value.

prompt_templates.title: Add Streaming Progress
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert my inference.sh task call to streaming mode. Handle status updates, partial output, completion, and errors without blocking the interface.

prompt_templates.title: Integrate a Secure Next.js Proxy
prompt_templates.prompt: Add an inference.sh proxy to my Next.js App Router project. Keep the API key server-side and include authentication, input validation, and rate limiting.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Controlled Agent Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a TypeScript inference.sh agent with typed tools and persistent sessions. Require approval for external actions, avoid eval, and define audit logging and failure handling.

output_examples.input: Add a secure inference.sh image generation task to a Node.js service.
output: Installation and private environment configuration steps.
A typed task flow with input validation and structured error handling.
Guidance for downloading the generated image with size and content checks.

output_examples.input: Plan a customer support agent that can notify Slack after approval.
output: An agent design with scoped tools and persistent session handling.
A confirmation step before sending the Slack notification.
Host restrictions, payload validation, redaction, and audit log recommendations.

best_practices: Keep API keys in private server environments and expose browser clients only through authenticated proxies.
Validate tool arguments and require approval for filesystem, code execution, and external network actions.
Pin dependencies, handle streamed failures, and record task identifiers for operational tracing.
anti_patterns: Do not evaluate model-generated expressions or tool arguments with eval.
Do not place inference credentials in NEXT_PUBLIC variables or browser bundles.
Do not allow unrestricted webhooks, package commands, or destructive tools without validation and approval.

faq.question: Does this skill require an inference.sh API key?
faq.answer: Yes. Direct SDK and server proxy examples require a valid inference.sh credential stored in a private server environment.

faq.question: Can I use the SDK in a browser?
faq.answer: Yes, but use a server proxy. Never include a private inference.sh API key in browser code or public environment variables.

faq.question: Does the skill support TypeScript?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers SDK types, typed tool parameters, error classes, type guards, and JSDoc annotations for JavaScript projects.

faq.question: Can it handle streaming results?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance covers asynchronous iteration, progress updates, partial output, cancellation concepts, and Server-Sent Events for web clients.

faq.question: Can agents call external tools?
faq.answer: Yes. Agents can use application, webhook, agent, and internal tools. Sensitive calls should use strict validation and human approval.

faq.question: Are the examples production ready?
faq.answer: No. Adapt authentication, authorization, rate limits, secret storage, input validation, monitoring, and error handling for your deployment.
